audit.whatIsWrong: The early-lane difficulty is built on Decisive Strike's silence 'interrupting your Flamespitter channel' and 'cancelling your damage window'. Flamespitter is not a channel.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Rumble torches opponents in front of him, dealing magic damage in a cone for 3 seconds.' There is no channel and no interrupt clause. A silence stops him casting a NEW spell; it does not switch off a Flamespitter that is already burning. That reverses the whole early-lane instruction — the answer is to have the cone already down before he closes to his 300-range Q, not to avoid casting it.
audit.corrected: Decisive Strike silences you out of casting, not out of a Flamespitter that is already burning. Get the cone down first and the 3 seconds tick through the silence.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 1-3 spike and the whys give Garen's early agency with no cooldowns attached, and the level-6 spike never mentions Demacian Justice at all.
audit.why: Decisive Strike is a flat 8s at every rank, Judgment 9 down to 6s, Courage 22 down to 12s, Demacian Justice 120/100/80s at 400 range. Flat 8s on his Q is the single most countable number in the lane and it was missing. Demacian Justice is an execute, so it becomes a hard threshold on your HP bar at 6 that nothing on the page warns about.
audit.corrected: Decisive Strike is a flat 8s; Courage is 22s at rank 1; Demacian Justice is 120s and executes from 400 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: The lane's defining interaction is absent: Decisive Strike breaks free of all slows on cast, so it cleanses your Electro Harpoon slow and your Equalizer slow. Also missing: Demacian Justice is an execute, so magic resist and armour do not reduce it.
audit.why: Riot's text for Decisive Strike says he 'gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him'. Rumble's only crowd control is slows, so Garen answers the whole of Rumble's kiting with one flat-8-second button. The correct sequence is therefore to harpoon AFTER he spends Q, not before, which buys 8 clean seconds. And an execute ignores resistances — the missing-interactions file flags this for Demacian Justice, and it is correct: buying MR does not raise the threshold, only health does.
audit.corrected: Decisive Strike breaks all slows on cast — harpoon him after he spends it and the slow sticks for 8 seconds. Demacian Justice executes, so MR does not raise the threshold; health does.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this matchup as having NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and the cooldown block says only 'Garen Courage: Damage reduction. Trade when down.'
audit.why: Every trading instruction on the page was untimed. Rewritten around the two numbers that matter: Decisive Strike's flat 8s, which gates his slow-break and his silence, and Courage's 22-to-12s, which gates his damage reduction.
audit.corrected: Trade in the 8s after Decisive Strike; commit the full pattern only once Courage is also spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] asserts 'the 30% damage reduction on his W'. That number is not in Riot's data.
audit.why: Riot's text for Courage says only 'a shield and tenacity for a brief moment followed by a lesser amount of damage reduction for a longer duration' — no percentage, and two distinct phases the page collapses into one. Quoting an invented 30% is exactly the kind of specific-sounding number a player will trust.
audit.corrected: Courage is a shield plus tenacity first, then weaker damage reduction for longer — no percentage asserted.

edits.after: Levels 1 through 3 belong to Garen, but not for the reason most players think. Decisive Strike is a flat 8 seconds and it breaks free of every slow on cast — your harpoons are the only crowd control you own, so that one button answers your whole kite. The silence stops you casting; it does NOT stop a Flamespitter that is already burning, since the cone runs 3 seconds once it is down. So the pattern is: cone first, then let him walk into it. Never open with a harpoon into his face — throw it in the 8 seconds after he spends Q and the slow finally sticks. At level 3 Courage arrives on 22 seconds, and if he shields before your burn ticks through, most of your damage is absorbed. Farm safe, keep the wave neutral, and stop expecting the free bully lane.
edits.before: Levels 1 through 3 belong to Garen. His Q silences you out of Flamespitter mid-channel and his passive regen means small poke trades net him more than they cost him. Do not walk your Q into him at level 1 expecting a free trade — he Q-spins back immediately and you lose the exchange. At level 2 you get Electro-Harpoon but his Q silence still cancels your damage pattern; only throw E to slow him away from your wave, never as an opener into his face. By level 3 your kit is online but his Courage goes up simultaneously — if he activates W before your Flamespitter ticks through, the damage reduction absorbs the bulk of your burst. Farm safely, keep the wave neutral, and accept that you are not bullying Garen the way you bully Nasus or Sion in this window.

edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are still Garen's — Perseverance undoes your chip unless something is touching him. Flamespitter's 3-second burn is the tool for that: every tick keeps his out-of-combat timer down, so the cone denies his regen better than a harpoon does. Count his Decisive Strike; in the 8 seconds after it, your slow holds and he cannot break it. At level 6 the math shifts off the map — The Equalizer across a river fight or dragon lane swings a skirmish harder than winning any 1v1 with Garen ever would. Ping your jungler for a 2v2 dragon side and aim the wall along the path, not on heads. Watch your own HP bar: Demacian Justice is a 120-second execute at 400 range.
edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are still Garen's — his passive sustain will undo the chip you accumulate unless you are consistently landing Danger Zone empowered Flamespitter on him AND denying his regen window with double Electro-Harpoon. The moment he stands still at the wave edge, throw both harpoons to deny the passive timer; if he chases, kite backward and melt him with Q. At level 6 the math shifts in your favor off the map — The Equalizer across a river fight or dragon lane will swing the skirmish harder than winning any 1v1 with Garen ever would. Ping your jungler for a 2v2 at dragon side and aim The Equalizer along the wall, not on heads — the burn ticks do the work.

notes: Two claims on this page were wrong in ways that reverse the advice. (1) The silence was said to interrupt a Flamespitter 'channel' — Riot's text has Flamespitter dealing damage in a cone for 3 seconds with no channel, so a silence only blocks the next cast; the fix is to lay the cone first. (2) whys[2] asserted '30% damage reduction' on Courage, a number that appears nowhere in Riot's data — Courage is described as a shield plus tenacity briefly, then a lesser damage reduction for longer. The lane's biggest missing interaction was Decisive Strike breaking free of all slows on cast: since slows are Rumble's only crowd control, a flat-8-second button answers the entire kite, and the correct sequence is to harpoon after he spends it. The _missing-interactions 'autoreset (Decisive Strike Q)' claim is not supported by Riot's text, which describes an empowered next attack rather than an attack reset, so it was not asserted. Courage's tenacity is irrelevant here — Rumble applies no stuns or roots for tenacity to shorten — so it was recorded but not written to the page.
